1 صَلَغَتِ البَقَرَةُ , and الشَّاةُ, (S, O, K,) aor.
صَلَغَ , (O,) inf. n. صُلُوغٌ, (S, O,) i. q. سَلَغَت, (S, O, K,) i. e. The bovine animal, and the sheep or goat, shed the tooth [next] behind that called the سَدِيس: (S and K in art. سلغ;) or bred its [tooth called the] نَاب: (K in that art. [in which see more]:) or صَلَغَ said of any cloven-hoofed animal, aor. and inf. n. as above, signifies he entered the sixth year: or, as some say, the fifth: this is the utmost of the ages thereof [that have verbs and epithets to denote them]: (Msb:) صُلُوغٌ (Mgh, Msb) in these animals (Msb) or in sheep or goats and animals of the bovine kind (Mgh) is like بُزُولٌ in camels. (Mgh, Msb.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
